title: Explanatory Supplement to the Astronomical Ephemeris and the American Ephemeris and Nautical Almanac (1961, reprint with 1973 added notes), section 10 Occultations, pp. 277-305
note: Read in full from the archive.org OCR text. Source of the occultation Besselian elements (T, H, Y, x', y'), the formulas for x and y and their rates, the station reduction with f, g and kn cos psi, the position angle, the a and b coefficients, the limiting parallels, the prediction limits, the k values 0.2725, 0.2724953 and 0.2725026, the reduction to delta-sigma, the limb correction arguments and section F on planetary occultations. Some equations are damaged in the OCR text.

title: Seidelmann, P. K. (ed.), Explanatory Supplement to the Astronomical Almanac (1992), section 9.4 Occultations (pp. 494-498), section 8.12 on k, and section 4.51 on historical UT1
note: Read sections 9.41, 9.42, the k paragraph of 8.12 and 4.51 in the archive.org OCR text. Source of equations 9.41-2 to 9.41-9 for the shadow on the Earth and the visibility map, the planetary occultation condition 9.42-1, the statement that ILOC in Tokyo reduced timings, and the 1982 adoption of k = 0.2725076 to conform to occultation work. Equation 9.41-8 is partly illegible in the scan.

title: Morrison, L. V. (1979). An analysis of lunar occultations in the years 1943-1974 for corrections to the constants in Brown's theory, the right ascension system of the FK4, and Watts' lunar-profile datum. MNRAS 187, 41-82
note: Read the method sections 2 to 4 in the ADS scan (OCR text). Source of the residual definition, the partial derivatives, the 932.58 arcsecond semidiameter relation, the refraction correction, the Watts-chart position-angle shift, the weights with their error components, the 0.49 arcsecond residual spread, and the corrections to mean longitude and the dynamical time scale before 1955.5.

title: Morrison, L. V. and Appleby, G. M. (1981). Analysis of lunar occultations II. Personal equation. MNRAS 196, 1005-1011
note: Read in full from the ADS scan. Source of the personal-equation expressions of Table 2 as functions of lunar elongation and star magnitude, the photoelectric control solution and the semidiameter correction of +0.04 arcseconds.

title: Herald, D. and Gault, D. et al. (2022). VizieR VI/132C, Archive of lunar occultation observations (1623 to the present), doc.txt and ReadMe
note: Read doc.txt in full and the ReadMe column list. Source of the custody history (HMNAO 1943, ILOC 1981 to 2008, IOTA from 2008), the observation counts and correction statistics, the reduction basis (DE440, Gaia EDR3 for most stars, deltaT splines, WGS84 conversion, polar motion, refraction, LOLA limb in a P,D frame at 0.01 degree spacing), and the default personal equations.

title: Herald, D. (2003). VizieR I/291, XZ Catalog of Zodiacal Stars (XZ80Q), ReadMe
note: Read the ReadMe. Source of the XZ origin at USNO in 1977 (Schmidt and Van Flandern), the 6 degree 40 arcminute zodiac band, the 32,221 original and 244,437 XZ80Q entries, the magnitude 12.0 completeness, and the double-star codes. The doc.txt history file could not be retrieved.

title: Herald, D. et al. (2016, updated). VizieR B/occ, Occultation light curves, ReadMe
note: Read the description section. Source of the video light-curve archive, the 0.3 to 0.4 arcsecond per second lunar motion, the 0.2 to 0.4 arcsecond per second normal limb rate and the 0.01 to 0.02 arcsecond resolution at video frame rate.

title: Robertson, J. (1940). Catalog of 3539 Zodiacal Stars for the Equinox 1950.0. Astronomical Papers prepared for the use of the American Ephemeris and Nautical Almanac, Vol. 10, Part 2
note: Not read. The catalogue's content, its 7.5 magnitude use limit and its role are described from ES 1961, Morrison and Appleby 1981 and the RASC Observer's Handbook lunar section.

title: Nugent, R. (ed.) (2007). Chasing the Shadow: The IOTA Occultation Observer's Manual. International Occultation Timing Association
note: Read chapter 4 (software), chapter 5 (grazes: geometry, elevation correction, limit-line shift, Occult graze profile, station placement, central graze time, double stars). Written by IOTA practitioners about their own methods.

title: Herald, D., Occult v4.2026 download page
note: Read. States the program's scope including lunar total and grazing occultations, the Gaia EDR3 subset to magnitude 16.0, optional UCAC4, and that the author reserves all rights to the source code.

title: Nather, R. E. and Evans, D. S. (1970). Photoelectric measurement of lunar occultations. I. The process. AJ 75, 575
note: Read in the ADS scan. Source of the MacMahon 1909 and Eddington history, the 42 ft first Fresnel zone, the 0.9 m per millisecond fringe rate, the sec factor of contact angle, Earth-rotation slowing, vector separation of doubles, and limb corrections as the 0.1 s limit of 1970 timings.

title: Richichi, A., Fors, O., Chen, W.-P. and Mason, E. (2010). New high-sensitivity, milliarcsecond resolution results from routine observations of lunar occultations at the ESO VLT. Astronomy & Astrophysics, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/201015325 (arXiv:1007.2611)
note: Read the abstract and introduction in the arXiv version, which the arXiv record says is to be published in A&A; the refereed journal version is the work cited. Source of the 0.75 m per millisecond fringe speed, the 20 to 40 milliarcsecond smearing size in the near infrared, and the 1 to 5 milliarcsecond upper limits.

title: Gaia Collaboration, Gaia DR3 documentation, section 4.1.7 Epoch propagation (chapter CU3 astrometry)
note: Read. Source of equations 4.8 to 4.17 for propagating position, parallax and proper motion under uniform rectilinear motion, the constant A_V = 4.740470464, and the treatment of unknown radial velocity.

title: ESA, Gaia Data Release 3 overview page
note: Read. Source of the 2016.0 reference epoch, the 2022 June 13 release date, and the positional and proper motion uncertainties.

title: RASNZ Occultation Section, Total occultations page
note: Read. An older page that still names ILOC as the receiver of timings. Source of the statement that a 0.1 s timing fixes the Moon's edge to about 80 m, and of the O-C residual in arcseconds as observers meet it.

title: British Astronomical Association, Lunar Section, Lunar occultations page
note: Read the first part. States that grazes are predicted in the BAA Handbook, that timings go to IOTA and are archived in VizieR VI/132A, and that LIMOVIE and GRAZPREP-4 are used.

title: Molteno, L., lunar-shadows (GitHub repository): DEM-corrected maps of lunar occultation limb projections
note: Read README, main.py and parts of observer.py and dem_correction.py. A third-party reimplementation with no documented validation. Uses a 1737.4 km lunar sphere, LOLA 118 m heights, a 6371 km spherical Earth for the first intersection and a WGS84 terrain step.
